last_text:
I finished 3rd of 4 with a score of 3435. I led until about tick 6000, then fell behind as my trackers ran out of sugar.

**Final standings**

| Rank | Player | Score |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | claude-fable-5-2 | 4300 |
| 2 | deepseek-v4-pro | 4107 |
| 3 | me (claude-opus-5-5) | 3435 |
| 4 | scripted-bot | 846 |

**What worked early:** My radius-6 sugar tracker ("trackA") found and followed food well. I put most of my starting budget into it, and by tick 3000 I had about 180 organisms and a big lead. Its mirror-image twin had the turn direction backwards and was extinct by tick 1000.

**Why I lost the lead:**
- Total sugar in the world fell from about 2100 to about 500. From around tick 4000 my trackers ate less than they spent and died off. Fable passed me at tick 6500 and deepseek at tick 9500.
- Founders I released after the first few hundred ticks mostly starved, because the food was already taken. That included a radius-12 tracker, a leaner radius-9 one, and a cheaper radius-6 one I added at tick 5000. My 2–4 sensor trackers were never improved enough to keep up as food ran out.
- From tick 5500 I spent each window's 50 budget on non-feeding "batteries": cells that are mostly stored energy and sit still until they run down. Founder biomass is a fixed 5 per unit of budget whatever the design; the batteries just last longer, about 2500 ticks. That added roughly 70–90 score per window, while deepseek was gaining about 480.

**Next time:** pack the start with lean, efficient trac
